title: Holiday plans
subtitle: Goodbye for now — I'm leaving on Tuesday
canDo: I can talk about fixed plans: I'm leaving on Tuesday.
I can say goodbye before a trip.
I can write an email about my holiday plans.
teacherNotes: Ünitenin son dersi: e-posta görevini (holiday plans) ödev verin. Geri bildirimde going to ve present continuous (future) kullanımına bakın.
Türkçede de "Yarın gidiyorum" dediğimiz için present continuous'ın gelecek anlamı Türklere kolay gelir. Zaman ifadesinin (tomorrow, on Tuesday) şart olduğunu vurgulayın.
going to / present continuous farkını fazla zorlamayın: A2'de ikisi de plan için kabul. Sadece saat ve yer belliyse present continuous daha doğal.
Konuşma: "What are you doing this weekend?" diye sorun; öğrenciler ajandalarına bakarak cevap versin.

sections.heading: Goodbye for now
sections.scene: Saturday, December 19th. Omar comes to Sam's café.

lines.text: Elif, I came to say goodbye. I'm flying to Amman tomorrow morning.

lines.text: Already? What time is your flight?

lines.speaker: omar
lines.text: I know. And you? When are you leaving for New York?

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: On Tuesday. Jake is picking us up at eight, and the band is playing in Brooklyn on Wednesday night.

sections.title: Read
sections.heading: Next stop: New York!
sections.intro: Elif's email to Zeynep on Monday night.
paragraphs: I'm packing my suitcase right now, and it's too small, of course! Tomorrow I'm leaving for New York with Lucas and his band.
Here's my plan. Tomorrow we're driving to the city. It's about four hours by car.
On Wednesday night, the band is playing in a small music café in Brooklyn. I'm selling their T-shirts at the door!
On Thursday, I'm going to visit two museums. Then I'm going to walk in the park and draw the old buildings.
On Christmas Day, everything is closed, so we're having a big lunch at Lucas's cousin's apartment. I'm making Turkish rice!
On New Year's Eve, I'm calling my family at five in the afternoon. It's midnight in Izmir then. Why don't you come to our house that night? Then I can say hello to you too.
What are you doing for the holidays? Write soon!

sections.title: Grammar: plans with -ing
look: The band **is playing** in Brooklyn **on Wednesday night**.

head: Form
Example
We use it for …
rows: a fixed plan (a time, a ticket, other people)
I**'m going to** visit two museums.

rules: For fixed plans, we often use **am / is / are + -ing**: *I'm meeting Sam at six.*
Use a future time word: **tomorrow, on Tuesday, next week, at eight**. Without it, the sentence means *now*.
**going to** is also OK for plans: *I'm going to fly on Sunday.*
examples: What are you doing this weekend?
We're having dinner at Omar's on Saturday.

support.tr: Present continuous (am / is / are + -ing), saati ve yeri belli planlar için de kullanılır: I'm flying to Amman tomorrow = Yarın Amman'a uçuyorum. Türkçede de "Yarın gidiyorum" deriz. Yalnız zaman ifadesi (tomorrow, on Tuesday) mutlaka olmalı; yoksa cümle "şu anda" anlamına gelir.
support.ar: نستخدم present continuous (am / is / are + ing) أيضًا للخطط المؤكّدة التي لها وقت ومكان: I'm flying to Amman tomorrow = سأسافر إلى عمّان غدًا. يجب أن نذكر كلمة زمن (tomorrow, on Tuesday)، وإلّا فهم المستمع أنّ الفعل يحدث الآن.

tr.note: Gelecek için -ing kullanırken de am / is / are gerekli. Soru: When are you …ing?
wrong: I leaving for New York on Tuesday.
right: I'm leaving for New York on Tuesday.

ar.note: في السؤال: أداة الاستفهام + are + الفاعل + الفعل مع ing.
wrong: Tomorrow I am travel to Amman.

sections.title: Write: My holiday plans

model.heading: To: Ana
text: Big news: Blue Monday is playing three concerts in New York next week!
We're leaving on Tuesday in Jake's car, and we're staying at our cousin Rafael's apartment.
Elif is coming with us. She's going to sell our T-shirts, and she's going to draw everything.
I'm not going to sleep much, but I don't care!
What are you doing for New Year's Eve? Are you going to the beach with Mom and Dad?

frame: For the holidays, I'm going to ___.
sections.prompt: Write an email to a friend about your plans for the next holiday (80 to 110 words). Use going to and -ing for fixed plans, and ask one question.
checklist: I use going to two times.
I use -ing for a fixed plan: I'm leaving on …
I use time words: on Tuesday, next week.
I ask a question about my friend's plans.
